wedge: public planned road-control/rally/event information + district or commute-corridor overlap => a next-morning impact answer with affected time window and official source links; avoid competing with live routing
last_material_result: One bounded distribution/substitute round found real pre-trip disruption pain but weakened the broad proactive-alert thesis. Public/news coverage repeatedly publishes next-day road controls, bus detours and station closures before major events or rallies, confirming that people need advance notice rather than only live traffic. However, broad real-time congestion and routing are already strong incumbent territory, and a nearby public-data consumer product (TEUM) already turns Seoul real-time city data into proactive Kakao alerts using scheduled backend infrastructure. No clear evidence surfaced that major navigation incumbents provide an equivalent mechanically derived 'tomorrow your saved commute is affected' answer, but the search surface is dominated by episodic news/official notices rather than obvious standalone search demand. Of the required three wedges: (1) generic district digest is weak because it duplicates city/news notices; (2) saved-corridor proactive alert has the strongest differentiated utility but likely requires persistent user state plus scheduled delivery, raising maintenance/platform dependency; (3) event/assembly next-morning alert can remain stateless/content-like but demand is episodic and monetization weak. Net: do not advance to BUILD; retain only a narrowed saved-corridor/district-impact concept for one feasibility/economics check before likely KILL or mutation.
economics: KRW0 research spend. Acquisition risk is now the dominant problem: generic disruption queries are served by official notices/news, while proactive saved-corridor value likely needs repeat delivery rather than SEO. Ads/affiliate monetization is weak at low episodic volume. A zero-backend district page could be cheap but poorly differentiated; a genuinely useful saved-corridor alert may require state/scheduling/channel infrastructure and therefore may fail the portfolio's near-zero-maintenance threshold.
next_checkpoint: Next run: test whether saved-corridor impact can be delivered without accounts/push or recurring paid infrastructure, e.g. deterministic shareable corridor URLs plus a daily generated static digest/RSS-like subscription surface. Quantify the minimum maintenance path and distribution mechanism. KILL if useful repeat delivery still requires account state, Kakao/push integration, or meaningful recurring backend work; if killed, mutate the same public-data substrate toward a stateless high-intent consumer action rather than another alert clone.
recommendation: KEEP for exactly one more feasibility/economics round, but downgrade confidence. Do not BUILD. Generic district/event digest is not differentiated enough; only the saved-corridor impact answer remains potentially defensible, and it must prove a zero/near-zero-maintenance delivery path.
